issues.legal_issue: A decree for permanent injunction based on a heritable property right may be enforced against the judgment-debtor’s legal representatives after the judgment-debtor’s death.
material_facts: The decree for permanent injunction was based on findings that the decree-holder had title to and possession of the disputed property and that the judgment-debtor had no right in it.
The right adjudicated was heritable and partible.
The judgment-debtor died before the decree was satisfied, and the legal representatives attempted to dispossess the decree-holder in breach of the injunction.
The decree-holder sought execution against the legal representatives.
issues.conclusion: The decree was enforceable against the judgment-debtor’s legal representatives. The executing court’s direction that they furnish an undertaking to abide by the decree was proper; if they failed to do so, the court could enforce the decree through a permissible mode.
issues.legal_principle: Section 50 CPC applies to decrees of all kinds, including permanent injunctions, and, read with Order XXI Rule 32 CPC, permits execution against the legal representatives of a deceased judgment-debtor. Section 146 CPC also permits proceedings against a person claiming under another. The maxim actio personalis moritur cum persona applies only to a limited class of actions and does not extinguish a decree where the right litigated is heritable. Girijanandini Devi v. Bijendra Narain Choudhary explains the limited scope of that maxim; Muthukaruppa Pillai v. Ganesan supports the survival and execution of an injunction decree concerning heritable rights.

predicates.injunction_execution_after_judgment_debt: The decree-holder sought to execute a permanent injunction after the judgment-debtor died before the decree was satisfied.
predicates.decree_concerns_heritable_property_right: The court based the injunction on a property right it found to be heritable and partible.
predicates.successors_interfered_with_protected_rig: The judgment-debtor’s legal representatives attempted to interfere with the right protected by the injunction.
predicates.decree_enforceable_against_judgment_debt: The permanent injunction may be enforced against the judgment-debtor’s legal representatives.

issues.definition: When execution is sought after a judgment-debtor’s death, the decree concerns a heritable property right, and the successors interfere with that protected right, the decree may be enforced against the judgment-debtor’s legal representatives.
